school.name: Northeastern University
school.about: The Northeastern University Dance Team was founded in 2003 by a group of Northeastern students passionate about dance and interested in supporting their school at a higher level. Since then, we have grown to be a spirit team staple in the athletic department. Our styles typically include hip-hop, jazz, and pom, with a strong underpinning of technique in all routines.
school.timeCommitment: We practice at the Marino Center on campus located on Huntington Ave and in the Cabot Physical Education Center. During the school year, we practice about 6 to 8 hours each week. In addition to practice times, we have a workout regimen of about 10 hours/week.
school.missionStatement: Our mission is to provide an avenue of performance for experienced dancers at various sporting events, as well as regional and nationally recognized competitions. We are highly dedicated to representing Northeastern University Athletics in a professional, positive, and energetic manner.
school.whatWeDo:
We are an official club sport, however, we practice, compete, and operate similarly to a collegiate varsity team. We practice 3 or 4 days each week, and work hard toward our prospective goals. We are a team of 24 girls from all majors, class years, and dance backgrounds.  As members, we are committed to dance and the mission of the team.

With Northeastern Athletics, we typically perform at the men and women's basketball team home games. At the end of each basketball season, we accompany the teams to their respective CAA tournaments. The tournaments vary in location each year but are typically held in major cities along the east coast. We have also had performances at various NU events and around Boston, including at the Boston Celtics. During competition season, we've performed at various competitions around New England and the US. We use these various venues to prepare for and compete in the National Dance Alliance Collegiate Championship that is held annually in Daytona Beach.

To join the team you must attend NUDT auditions, which are held twice a year. Auditions take place once in early September, before the season starts, in April, after the season ends, and in July, for incoming Freshman. You will be asked to perform a series of progressions, leaps, and turns. You will then perform a short combination that the choreographer will teach you in front of the judges. You will be evaluated on your skills and abilities as a dancer.  You may or may not be asked to answer questions about yourself.  There is no need to prepare your own combination. If you are unable to attend auditions, you may submit a video.

school.about: The Bradley Bravettes Dance Team is a collegiate dance team made up of dedicated dancers. Their style of dance usually consists of Jazz, Pom and Hip Hop. school.missionStatement: The Bravettes originally date back to the 80s, where they danced as a team until they were disbanded near the end of the decade. Bradley went for many years without an official dance team until 2003, when Jill Crouch and Nina Butler convinced Bradley University to allow them to start the Bravettes again. The first tryouts were held in 2004, and the original team was only nine dancers, with Kara Girsch as the first four year member of the team . Before the  Markin Recreation Center was built, the Bravettes bused to practice facilities at various studios in Pekin and Morton. Once Markin was completed in 2008, the Bravettes moved their practices back on campus. Over the years, the Bravettes have performed at women's basketball games, men's soccer games, and men's basketball games. In 2023, captains Izzy Fontane and Abby Poulos earned the team the club sport designation. The Bravettes are a resilient student organization dedicated to representing the spirit of Bradley.

We value the individuality of our dancers, as each member is an essential asset to our program.

While we don’t hold strict physical requirements for auditions on our team, listed below are skills that our judging panel looks for and are encouraged to be worked on:

• Double/triple/quad pirouettes (right and left)

• Variety of turn combinations in second

• Leg extensions/turns

• Leaps (right, left, and center) and turning disk

• Kip-Up and head spring

• Any other tumbling/flexibility skills (front/side aerials, rubberbands, back handsprings/tucks, etc.)

Even if you do not have all of the above skills, we encourage everyone to audition for the team! We love to see committed dancers who are willing to learn and have great performance skills!

school.name: University of Wisconsin- Eau Claire
school.benefits: While the UWEC Dance Team is a competitive team and holds themselves to the same standards as an athletic team,  we are considered a club sport by the university, which means we aren’t part of the athletic department. We receive some funds from a state allocation for club teams based on GPA, volunteer hours, and attendance at leadership and other events on campus, but we are otherwise a completely self-funded team. Upon earning a spot on the team, dancers will need to pay a team fee of $1000, due approximately one week after auditions conclude, to help cover the costs of UDA camp, UDA Home Routine choreography, UDA Home routine costumes, poms, and summer practice space costs. The rest of our funds are raised through fundraisers we organize. Team members are expected to attend and/or participate in all team fundraisers. It costs approximately $5000 per season, per dancer, to be part of the team, which includes the $1000 team fee and all other associated costs, like costumes, shoes, makeup, competition fees, airfare, and lodging. Fundraising accounts for 30-85% of that each season, depending on the success of each fundraiser. Any funds not raised are out of pocket expenses for dancers on the team
school.about: The UW-Eau Claire Blugold Dancers make up an organization designed to perform at sporting and community events. The styles they specialize in are jazz and hip hop. They compete against other college dance teams at various competitions and hold an annual high school dance team competition and clinic here at UW-Eau Claire. The team members are hardworking, dedicated, and talented individuals who express interest in dancing at the collegiate level.
school.timeCommitment: Team members are treated like student athletes, and are expected to act as such. The time commitment expected of team members is significant. Dancers are expected to manage their time in a way that school, work, family, and personal obligations do not interfere with team obligations.
school.whatWeDo: The UW- Eau Claire Dance Team and their coaching staff have an intentionally set team culture by implementing team values and standards, and they have a collective agreement to consistently and predictably effectuate and follow them. In order to elevate the UW- Eau Claire Dance Team program, the voluntary commitment from all team members to follow the team values and standards is a necessity. These values and standards are promises to teammates and coaches displayed through behavior at all times- in and out of uniform, at all practices, performances, appearances, fundraisers, and events. The strength of the team is determined by the commitment of all team members and coaches to the values and standards set forth.

school.whatWeDo:
Gold Team
The Golden Bulls Dance Club's Gold Team is a collegiate-level competitive dance group, currently ranked 3rd in D1 Jazz at The College Classic Nationals. As an entirely student-led team, throughout the school year, we focused on preparing and perfecting our dance piece for Nationals in April. With bi-weekly practices, conditioning, and open classes, Gold members train 6 hours a week by attending the two competition practices and one weekly open class. Beyond Nationals, Gold members also perform locally with our Green Team and participate in our annual Spring Showcase.

Green Team
The Golden Bulls Dance Club's Green Team is a performance-based group that showcases fun dance performances at local events throughout the USF and Tampa community. Last year, we performed at USF's Homecoming Parade, the Florida State Fair, Dance Marathon at USF, and more. While some dance experience is beneficial, our Green Team welcomes any passionate and dedicated student who loves to perform, regardless of their level of training. In addition to local performances, Green Team members also participate in our annual Spring Showcase.

school.about:
Missouri Valley College is a small private liberal arts college  in Marshall, Missouri offering both undergraduate and graduate degree programs. We are located 1.5 hours east of Kansas City and 2.5 hours west of St. Louis. MVC is a member of the Heart of America Conference within the NAIA. As a member of the NAIA we are able to offer dance, cheer, twirl and color guard members athletic scholarships averaging around 45% of the total cost of attendance when athletic, academic, character and needs based aid are all combined together (this does not include grants received through FAFSA).  

The team is under the direction of  Head Coach Kristen Revis. She has big plans for this team! She is going into her 24th year of coaching at the high school and collegiate levels, as well as teaching at dance studios within the St. Louis area. Past schools include Lindenwood University, Marquette HS, Whitfield Schools, Charmette Academy of Dance, Dynamic Edge Dance Center, Motion House and Emily Jane’s. She also judges for KAR Brands, DanceOut and previously for Varsity Brands. (Bio Available on MoVal.edu.)

Missouri Valley Dance Team is comprised of 16 dancers for the 25-26 season. In the 26-27 season there will be a second team added to the program. Both teams will have approximately 25 dancers on each roster. 

The dance team is blessed to have a full size air conditioned gym and dance classroom for practice, dedicated strength and conditioning coach focusing on injury prevention for dancers, as well as conditioning geared towards higher elevation for leaps and jumps and stronger turns, full time athletic trainer, as well as many other amenities and benefits for the dancers. 


If you are interested in learning more please fill out the dance athletic questionnaire or email Coach Revis. You can also schedule  a campus tour and meet the team and Coach Revis! She would love to talk with you!

When not performing at games the team can be found within the community volunteering at different events and making appearances at most campus events. They have at least one team bonding event a month and also fundraise to cover the costs not covered by MVC. The goal is to keep out of pocket costs as low as possible!

Mahr has been coaching the dance team at Sioux City West High School since 2020.  She started as an assistant before moving into the head coach position.  Mahr has also been a coach at 5678! Dance Studio in McCook Lake, S.D. since 2021.
 
"Madison Mahr's appointment as head coach of our new cheer and dance programs marks an exciting chapter for Briar Cliff University athletics," said University President Dr. Matthew Draud. Mahr was a member of the Morningside Dance team.  She served as team captain and helped the Mustangs win the NAIA National Championship in 2022.  Mahr has a Coaching Certificate from Western Iowa Tech CC and a B.S. in Marketing from Morningside.
 
"We are extremely excited to add competitive dance and competitive cheer programs to our sport offerings," said Executive Director of Athletics Tim Jager.  "We look forward to watching Madison build these programs as BCU provides more opportunities for dance and cheer athletes to compete in the GPAC and nationally."

These scholarships have specifications and information will be given as soon as a Strutter is selected to the team. Scholarship distribution can be given out on average anywhere from $200-$3,000 once per year. Please note these amounts are distributed late August after all Strutter dues and fees are due.
school.about:
The Texas State Strutters is the FIRST precision dance team formed at a four-year university and is currently the largest in the nation. For 65 years, Strutters have served as ambassadors for Texas State University on state, national, and international levels with performances in 27 countries spanning 4 continents.

This exceptional organization was founded by Ms. Barbara Guinn Tidwell; renowned as a legend in drill team history. Mrs. Tidwell served as director/choreographer for 37 years. From 1997-2013, the director/choreographer of Strutters was former Strutter Captain Mrs. Susan Angell-Gonzalez. Former Strutter Tammy Fife served as the director/choreographer from 2013-2020. Currently, the Strutters are under the direction of another former Strutters Captain, Selina Flores Lloyd. 

The Strutters have also represented Texas State University as the first U.S. dance team to perform in the People's Republic of China. Other highlights include: three Presidential Inaugural Parades, numerous NFL & NBA halftime performances, performances on the Royal Caribbean's Mariner of the Seas and Liberty of the Seas, the McDonald's Thanksgiving Parade in Chicago, and the Dunkin' Donuts Thanksgiving Day Parade in Philadelphia. They have made televised appearances on MTV's Total Request Live, a national television commercial for Coca-Cola, five different movies, "America's Got Talent", and the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade.
 
Aside from excellence in performances and dance, the organization takes pride in helping young women develop communication skills, character, and confidence. While hosting annual intensives, masterclasses, and workshops, the Strutters serve as exemplary role models to thousands of high school dance team members across Texas. The Texas State Strutters has brought much entertainment, pride, and recognition to Texas State University and will continue the tradition of excellence for years to come.
school.timeCommitment: Strutters practice Monday, Wednesday, & Friday 6-10AM. Classes must be scheduled around practice. Performances vary based on each semester. All Strutters are required to attend all shows and practices for home football games and sign up for a number of home basketball games.
school.whatWeDo:
The Strutters are a performance based dance team. Instead of competing we perform at all football and basketball home games as well as a few baseball and volleyball games. The Strutters hold 4 annual shows a year; Meet the Strutters, Fall Spectacular, Holiday Spectacular, & Strutters Spectacular where we perform a variety of dance genres. Every year we have a special performance trip. It could range between traveling to a bowl game, performing in a local or national parade, or traveling internationally for a performance.
We have two specialty groups; pom squad and jazz elite. These two groups are in addition to the team after auditioning for Strutters. These groups have more performance and appearance opportunities throughout the year. The Strutters serve as ambassadors for Texas State Athletics as well as Texas State University.

school.about:

Each dancer practices 4x a week whether it's a full team practice or competition/game day practice.  All dancers perform on the sideline and at halftime of all home football games, while the game day team takes on the majority of men’s and women’s home basketball games (the full team will do larger scale games).  

MCDT competes yearly at both the regional and national level.  Our Game Day team competes in a hip hop routine at New England Regionals in February.  A select number of Game Day members also compete in Division 1 Game Day at NDA College Nationals in Daytona Beach, FL.  The competitive team competes in Division 1 Jazz and Team Performance at Nationals.  2024 was our first year in Division 1 and we are able to proudly say MCDT is a Top 5 Division 1 Team.

The team performs at numerous pep rallies and campus events throughout the year.
 
The HighTechs dance team consists of a group of people who enjoy dancing, generating school spirit, and entertaining fans at Virginia Tech Intercollegiate Athletic events. The audience is treated to unique choreography that includes fast transitions, jumps, leaps, and turns. Their timeout and halftime performances demonstrate a variety of styles, including jazz, pom, and hip hop.
 
Practices focus on choreography and learning and perfecting technique. Members of the HighTechs are also encouraged to choreograph routines for performances at games and pep rallies. The HighTechs practice between eight and twelve hours a week and are required to attend workouts with the strength and condition coach. Members who make the nationals team are required to attend additional practices depending on the time of year.

school.about:
UMD is located on Lake Superior in Northeast Minnesota. The campus is made up of more than 50 buildings, and most are connected by concourses or hallways known as the “tunnels”. 

The city of Duluth is unique with many features including the largest fresh water lake, light houses, the aerial lift bridge, park point beach, walking and hiking trails, local restaurants and shops, and much more! Duluth is full of many adventures for all four seasons.

The UMD Dance Team is rooted in the community. We make many appearances at local dance shows, elementary schools, nursing homes, races, and much more!

Each year, we seek committed, confident and passionate dancers to join our program. As representatives of UMD, team members embody excellence in academics, athletics and performance at the national level. While being a UMD dancer offers numerous opportunities, it demands significant dedication. Please review our program's time commitment carefully. Your college decision is pivotal, and we are honored by your interest in UMD!

All costumes, food on the road, coach bus, hotel, team supplies... everything is covered out of our team budget, meaning no extra expense or extreme fundraising is put on your plate. (You have enough going on!) Did we mention the best part? We have DANCE TEAM SCHOLARSHIPS. Yes, dancers are athletes. Yes, you deserve a scholarship for the hard work you put into our team.
school.about:
If you're looking for a FUN, ORGANIZED, COMPETITIVE college dance team experience, VUDT is your team! A Full-Time Head Coach, 2 Assistant Coaches, Athletic Training Staff, Strength and Conditioning Training Staff, a Team Chaplain and Athletics Department Administration Staff are all here to support our team of 30+ VARSITY ATHLETES.

Our team performs at home games, competes and Regional and National competitions, and performs our annual Guy/Girl routine with the Viterbo Baseball Team. Past accomplishments include Runner Up at WACPC Collegiate Hip Hop championship, 4X NAIA National Qualifiers, Highest Student-Athlete GPA winner Bailey Johnson (2024), NAIA Dancer of the Year and Viterbo Female Athlete of the Year, Nyah Brooks (2023). 

Want to learn more? Let's chat!

Our coaches prioritize efficiency and organization to minimize stress on our team members - so YOU can enjoy being a student-athlete. We work hard and ENJOY THE SMALL & BEAUTIFUL MOMENTS.

school.name: Northern Arizona University
school.about:
The NAU Dance Team is truly involved in the University. Our first priority is to provide spirit to the various sports teams that are on campus. We dance at NAU football and basketball games, and participate in various athletic games and events to provide support and spirit. The team also participates in two National Dance Competitions, Universal Dance Association (UDA) and United Spirit Association (USA) at the D1 level. The student athletes that participate in this program are held to a high standard both academically and professionally. They must attend weekly practices, workouts, attend all games and events, and present themselves in a positive way as they represent the University. 
	
Prospective members MUST have a positive work ethic, respect for self and others, and be dedicated to representing the University as well as the team in a professional manner. We ask that you be able to commit to ALL team practices, performances and games. All members must be in good physical condition to properly handle the intense physical training and performance schedule while maintaining this fitness level throughout the season.	
			
As members of the NAU Dance Team, you have the opportunity to be involved in the NAU community, and support the Lumberjacks. This is an extremely supportive and involved team in and out of team practices and performances. We are excited to see that you are interested in our program.

Dance Team at NAU, a Division I team, competes at the national level yearly at UDA Nationals in Florida. The Dance Team will teach new routines, collegiate-level skills, and audition preparation strategies. The dancers in attendance may choose to try-out for the team in April, where if they are selected, must be admitted to NAU before their membership on the team can be actualized.

Our mission is to uplift and energize our campus, support fellow athletic teams, and serve our community through meaningful involvement. school.about:
Dordt is a Christian, faith based school, and we are located in Northwest Iowa, right in the heart of the Midwest! 😃 God created us to glorify him in everything we do. That's why Dordt wants to help you discover your gifts, embrace your role in God's story, and learn to love your neighbor like Jesus did.

As a top Christian university, Dordt offers a vibrant faith community in addition to outstanding academic programs designed to equip you for a lifetime of service in the kingdom of God. And that's what you were made for.

Our team is a part of the NAIA, which means that all of our dancers on our team are able to received athletic scholarships for being on the dance teams, and they have almost zero out of pocket extra costs for them to be on the team!! We get the opportunity to perform at game days at all home football and basketball games, and we also get the opportunity to travel and compete at about 8-10 different competitions throughout the year. This past year we also traveled to Orlando, FL to compete at the DTU College Classic, and we came home as NATIONAL CHAMPIONS! 

We recruit dancers and offer roster spots to incoming athletes year round. The first step that recruits should do, is to fill out our recruit prospect form! https://godordt.com/sb_output.aspx?form=9

If you are interested in applying for a dance scholarship, as well as a dance roster spot, please send Coach Mel Knobloch (mel.knobloch@dordtd.edu) some videos that demonstrate your best skills and abilities and Coach Mel will reach out with an offer for you! There are no set required elements that are needed for these videos.  

We love to host recruits on campus, and we invite you to join us anytime during the year to sit in on a practice, join us for a game day, and even stay overnight in the dorms with current dance and cheer members! We also have a really great reimbursement option for those that are traveling from a distance! To sign up for a campus visit, please go to www.dordt.edu/visit

We can't wait to meet you and help you navigate your future college decisions, and help you to become a future Dordt Defender Dancer! 

If you have any questions, please don't hesitate to reach out to Coach Mel Knobloch at mel.knobloch@dordt.edu

i.	Be a leader, a servant, a role model, and a great teammate

i.	Be respectful of your parents, family, professors, coaches, peers and God

school.name: University of Redlands
school.benefits: Dancers on the University of Redlands Dance Team gain a wide range of personal, professional, and performance benefits. Members have the opportunity to perform at football and basketball games, participate in campus events and rallies, and, for the first time this season, compete at the collegiate level. The team offers a supportive and inclusive environment where dancers can grow as leaders, build strong friendships, and develop valuable skills like communication, time management, and confidence. Dancers receive custom team gear, take part in media day photoshoots, and are featured on our social media platforms. The team also hosts workshops and clinics with guest choreographers to enhance technique in styles such as jazz, hip hop, and pom. As ambassadors for the university, our dancers represent Redlands spirit with pride, both on campus and in the community.
school.about: The University of Redlands Dance Team, established in 2022, serves as the official spirit and performance team of the university. As a proud representation of campus energy and talent, we perform at football and basketball games to promote school spirit and community. This season marks an exciting milestone as we prepare to compete for the first time in program history.
school.timeCommitment: The University of Redlands Dance Team requires a strong commitment from its members to maintain performance quality and team unity. Sideline team members attend early morning practices three days a week to prepare for football and basketball game performances. Dancers who are part of the competitive team have two additional practices each week focused on choreography, technique, and competition prep. During the season, dancers can also expect to perform at 1–2 games per week. While the schedule is rigorous, it fosters discipline, teamwork, and growth—both as dancers and as leaders on campus.
school.missionStatement: The University of Redlands Dance Team is dedicated to fostering school spirit, unity, and pride through high-energy performances and positive representation of our university. We strive to build a supportive and inclusive team environment that empowers dancers to grow as athletes, leaders, and ambassadors—both on and off the field. Through performance, competition, and community engagement, we aim to inspire Bulldog pride in everything we do.
school.whatWeDo: The University of Redlands Dance Team performs at home football and basketball games, campus events, and spirit rallies to promote school pride and energize the Bulldog community. school.name: Tulane University
school.about: The Tulane University Dance Team is a Division 1A collegiate spirit program that performs at all home football games, men's and women's basketball games, and competes nationally at NDA College Nationals in both Jazz and Hip Hop divisions. We also represent Tulane at campus events and in the greater New Orleans community, including performances in the city’s iconic Mardi Gras parades. Our dancers train year round through practices, workouts, and team travel, building strong foundations in technique, performance, and leadership. We welcome talented and driven dancers from all backgrounds who are ready to grow as athletes and performers while being part of a supportive and high-energy team culture.

Academics remain a top priority, and team members are expected to manage their time effectively to maintain both their academic and athletic commitments.

We are committed to upholding the highest standards of school spirit and competitive excellence through dedication, discipline, and teamwork. Our dancers are expected to maintain strong academic standing and demonstrate a balance between athletic commitment and academic success. We strive to create a supportive environment where dancers grow both on and off the floor—performing at athletic events, competing nationally, and representing Tulane within the vibrant New Orleans community.

The Club Dance Team and Dance Team participate in some performances and activities together and have some events and performances as separate teams. As a CSB Dance Team or Club Dance Team member, student-athletes are a representative not only of the team, but also the entire college. 
 
The proud tradition of the CSB Dance Team is carried on by dedicated student-athletes who devote many hours every week to practices, games, special appearances, camps and competitions. We are always looking for skilled and talented athletes, as well as well-rounded students, who embrace the ability to be coached. CSB Dance Team and Club Dance Team members must be able to find a healthy balance between athletics, school, family, and friends. They also attend practices in December and January prior to their UDA National competition in Orlando, FL. The Dance Team is a great opportunity for any Bennie Dancer that wants to compete at a collegiate level. Dancers who are studying abroad during the spring semester and have a departure date after UDA Nationals are eligible to participate on the Dance Team. Those who have departure dates before the UDA Nationals will not be allowed to be on the Dance Team.

school.about:
WM Elite is a nationally competitive dance team designed for dancers who are ready to push themselves to the next level. While you still get the college dance team experience, our program focuses on preparing dancers for life after college whether that’s training in L.A., joining a company, or auditioning for major industry opportunities.

We’re heading into our third season as WM Elite, having launched in 2022 and we’re so excited to continue growing, evolving, and creating opportunities for our dancers.

Our choreography leans into hard-hitting , commercial, and technically advanced styles, giving our dancers the versatility they need to succeed in today’s dance industry. We believe in training with purpose while fostering a culture of support, confidence, and passion.

Last season, we were proud to work with Jordan Lorenger (L.A. Clippers dancer), Dakayla Wilson (So You Think You Can Dance runner-up), and Dominic Franco (Kansas City Chiefs alum, Texas Tech alum, 3x national champion, and owner of Dominate Technique).

This season, we’ve already brought in incredible talent like Brian Friedman, Kelly Sweeney, Lauren Yakima, Dakayla Wilson and Elle Dimos with more exciting guests to come.

At DTU Nationals last year, we were the only club team to make it to finals, standing alongside top collegiate programs from across the country.

If you’re looking for a team that pushes you, supports you, and truly prepares you for what’s next WM Elite is the place to be. We can’t wait to meet you, grow with you, and watch you shine.
school.timeCommitment:

As we approach nationals and enter peak season, our commitment increases to 3–5 practices per week to ensure we’re fully prepared to perform at a high level.

We understand that dancers often balance school, work, and other responsibilities, and we strive to maintain a structured schedule that supports both excellence and balance.
school.missionStatement: At WM Elite, our mission is to empower dancers through elite level training, impactful mentorship, and industry focused opportunities. school.about:
Roosevelt's dance program captured the first national title in program history Saturday in the hip hop division of the National Dance Association College Nationals in Daytona Beach, Fla.

The Lakers proved in Friday's preliminaries that they were poised to improve upon the third-place finishes from the last two years. Roosevelt led by more than five points after that first round of dancing, and the lead only grew in Saturday's final. The Lakers improved their raw score by more than 0.5 points in the final to create a nearly one-point bump in the event score to capture the title.
school.whatWeDo: "Back in the spring of 2020, I was given the honor of starting the cheer and dance programs at Roosevelt. At the time, with over a decade of college coaching experience, seeing a collegiate dance team in Chicago win a national title felt like a dream—one I wasn't sure I'd witness in my own career," spirit coordinator and Roosevelt dance coach Lindsay Jones said. "But I was determined to build something strong, something lasting. With only six returners this season, our team rose to the challenge—welcoming new members, building mental and physical grit, and keeping each other grounded in our mission. Our goal was never just to win—it was to get better every day. 'Progress over perfection' was our mantra. If just one detail improved each run, that was a win in itself."

1. Persistence: Members must put forth effort to better themselves each day and to reach their 	goals.

school.about:
Hi there! My name is Stephanie Brant, and I serve as the Director of Spirit Programs and Head Dance Coach at Greenville University. I’m so glad you’re interested in learning more about our program!
I’ve been a head collegiate coach for 14 years, and I’m passionate about developing well-rounded collegiate dancers. Our team focuses on all aspects of college dance—jazz, pom, hip-hop, and game-day—and we perform at home football and men’s basketball games while also competing nationally.
We’ve had strong competitive success in recent years. In 2022 and 2023, we competed in the game-day division at NCA/NDA Nationals. More recently, we’ve competed in Small Coed, Super Spirit Showdown, and Hip-Hop at The College Classic, earning Top 5 national rankings, including 2nd in Small Coed, 2nd in Super Spirit Showdown, and 5th in Hip-Hop. This year, we’re also excited to add Team Performance to our competition lineup.
Greenville University is a small, private Christian college in Illinois, located about 50 miles from St. Louis, Missouri. Our campus has a warm, close-knit community feel while still being close to a big city with lots of fun weekend options.
Our team typically practices 3–4 days a week, and we’re supported by both an acro coach (1.5 hours weekly at a gymnastics facility) and a strength & conditioning coach (2 days a week for an hour). We emphasize a strong team culture through monthly bonding activities, Bible studies (8–10 per semester), and our end-of-practice positivity circle, where we take time to encourage one another and end each practice on a positive note.
The university covers most of our team expenses, and we participate in fundraising to help with additional travel and competition costs.
I personally recruit all team members, so rather than a traditional tryout, your “audition” will be through the videos you submit. You’re welcome to send me any skills, routines, or your common dance application video, and I’ll evaluate your submission for both team placement and scholarship opportunities.
I look forward to connecting with you and sharing more about what it means to be part of the Pantherette Dance Team family!
Warmly,

Coach Stephanie Brant
Director of Spirit Programs & Head Dance Coach
Greenville University
